integrity_notes: The theorem has an analytical proof; finite enumerations are supporting checks, not infinite-horizon certificates.
The original source publication date was taken from the dated initial Optimization Online posting rather than a later arXiv revision.
scientific_limitations: Specific to an independently validated, fixed-unit-step comparison on two noninterpolating quadratic losses, not an entire adaptive preconditioning algorithm.

The source relative-gradient-noise hypothesis fails at the population optimum; its function-value condition need not fail on the discrete set of reachable states. The finding therefore does not contradict the source convergence theorem.
The exact numerical constants depend on the symmetric two-label model and strict tie rejection.
Potentially related results under older stochastic line-search or sequential testing terminology have not been excluded by exhaustive literature review.
title: A sharp logarithmic validation-budget frontier for a noisy descent safeguard
